one_line: Father-and-son Kadamba rulers leading the 5th–6th century military and political revival from Banavasi and Halasi.

appearance.age_look: Mrigeshavarma appears in his early 40s with a solid warrior’s build; Ravivarma appears in his late 20s with a lean, athletic frame.
appearance.face: Both share an oval face with straight nose and medium-brown Deccan complexion; Mrigeshavarma’s jaw is slightly squarer with a neat moustache and faint forehead lines, default expression focused and stern; Ravivarma’s features are finer with no facial hair and a calm, alert expression that softens into a slight, diplomatic half-smile.
appearance.hair: Mrigeshavarma’s hair is black, tied in a high warrior topknot with a few short strands at the temples, topped by a simple golden kadamba-mukut style circlet with a small central leaf motif; Ravivarma’s black hair is pulled back into a low, tidy topknot under a slimmer golden circlet band with a tiny sun-disc front ornament.
appearance.costume: Both wear early medieval Deccan royal attire: Mrigeshavarma has a rich deep-red silk upper cloth (uttariya) diagonally across his chest over a fitted, knee-length off-white cotton tunic and a mustard-yellow dhoti wrapped tightly to mid-calf with neat front pleats, secured by a broad brown leather belt; he wears plain golden armlets, a single short gold necklace, slim gold bangles, and simple brown leather sandals, with a sturdy rectangular wooden shield slung on his back; Ravivarma’s costume echoes but refines his father’s—he wears a pale-cream tunic, a muted teal silk uttariya across both shoulders like a courtly shawl, and a soft light-ochre dhoti falling just above the ankles with a slightly looser wrap, tied with a slimmer dark-brown belt; his jewellery is slightly more ornate but still restrained—slender gold armlets with a leaf motif, a double-strand gold necklace, and a single ring on his right hand, and he also wears brown sandals; both have modest, era-appropriate coverage with no bare torso, and their garments are plain-weave or simple silk with minimal patterning, suggesting practical royal dress suited to campaign and court.
appearance.signature: Mrigeshavarma holds a long, straight iron sword with a simple cross-guard and slightly flared pommel in his right hand, while Ravivarma carries a rolled copper-plate charter tied with a red cord in his left hand, both standing together as a paired image.

ref_desc: Mrigeshavarma and Ravivarma are a father–son pair with medium-brown oval faces and black topknots under simple gold circlets, wearing cream tunics, deep-red or teal uttariyas and mustard/light-ochre dhotis with gold jewellery, the father gripping a plain iron sword and the son holding a rolled copper-plate charter, all in deep red, mustard yellow, muted teal, cream and gold tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of two Kadamba rulers, Mrigeshavarma and his son Ravivarma, standing side by side in early 6th century Deccan royal attire, fully and modestly clothed. Mrigeshavarma is a solidly built man in his early forties with a medium-brown Deccan complexion, an oval face with a straight nose, neatly trimmed moustache, and a focused, stern expression. His black hair is tied in a high warrior topknot, topped by a simple golden circlet resembling a kadamba-mukut with a small central leaf motif. He wears a fitted off-white cotton tunic that covers his torso and upper arms, a deep-red silk uttariya draped diagonally across his chest and over one shoulder, and a tightly wrapped mustard-yellow dhoti reaching mid-calf with crisp front pleats, secured by a broad brown leather belt. He has plain gold armlets, a short gold necklace, slim gold bangles, and simple brown leather sandals; a sturdy rectangular wooden shield hangs on his back, and he firmly holds a long, straight iron sword with a simple cross-guard and slightly flared pommel in his right hand. Ravivarma stands slightly behind and to the side, a lean, athletic man in his late twenties with a similar medium-brown oval face, finer features, no facial hair, and a calm, alert expression with a hint of a diplomatic half-smile. His black hair is pulled into a low, tidy topknot under a slimmer gold circlet with a tiny sun-disc front ornament. He wears a pale-cream tunic, a muted teal silk uttariya draped across both shoulders like a shawl, and a light-ochre dhoti wrapped more loosely to just above the ankles, tied with a slimmer dark-brown belt; his jewellery is modest but slightly more ornate, with slender gold armlets bearing a leaf motif, a double-strand gold necklace, a single ring on his right hand, and brown sandals. He carries a rolled copper-plate charter tied with a red cord in his left hand, held forward as a symbol of royal grants and claims. Emphasize the consistent colours—deep red, mustard yellow, muted teal, cream, and gold—keeping the style shonen-anime but all clothing, ornaments and weapons historically plausible for 5th–6th century Banavasi and Halasi, with no exposed torsos and a clear contrast between the warrior-father with sword and shield and the younger ruler with charter scroll.
